slides.title: B · Convergence (v3 fits)
bullets: Every objective went one way only. The v3 neural fits stopped at a 1,500 s limit; the v4 refits use a 250-iteration budget.

slides.title: B · Tests

slides.title: D · Real-data design and evaluations
bullets: 1000 cells = 4 libraries (2F, 2M) × 5 hemilineages × 50; 100 HVGs; raw UMI counts from premn_24h; 36 (λ, k) fits.

slides.title: D · Data: counts and binarized matrices
bullets: Cells sorted hemilineage → library → depth; genes clustered.
Y≥1 density 0.487; Y≥2 density 0.373.
Hemilineage blocks are obvious by eye; library stripes are not.

slides.title: D · Fitted probabilities across prior strength × rank
bullets: k=1: one gene-propensity axis.
Small λ + large k: P → 0/1, copies Y (overfit; held-out NLL 2.8).
λ=10, k=20: smooth, block-structured probabilities; best held-out NLL 0.479.

slides.title: D · Log counts, binary Y and inferred Bernoulli probabilities
bullets: Same cell order (hemilineage → library → depth) and gene order in every panel. P̂ turns each 0/1 into a probability: hemilineage blocks become sharp, and detection noise within a block is smoothed.

slides.title: D · Zoom: 60 cells × 40 genes, entry by entry
bullets: 12 cells per hemilineage from one library. High counts map to high P̂; isolated 1s in low-probability genes (and 0s in high-probability ones) are read as sampling noise. The compact fit (λ=1, k=5) is smoother; the CV-best fit (λ=10, k=20) keeps more cell-level detail.

slides.title: D · Grid overview
bullets: Train likelihood rises with k and falls with λ; held-out metrics peak at strong shrinkage with generous rank.

slides.title: D · Held-out entry CV: λ is the real complexity knob
bullets: Best: λ=10, k=20 (NLL 0.479, AUC 0.858) vs additive cell+gene logistic 0.544 / 0.800. λ≥30 collapses; λ=100 → U=V=0. Weak priors are over-confident (d).

slides.title: D · Information content: P ranks expression level from binary data
bullets: Within detected entries, median gene-wise ρ(P, counts) = 0.30 (0.28 after removing depth) vs 0.03 for a depth × abundance reference; P saturates above ~3 UMI.

slides.title: D · Biology vs batch on real data
bullets: Hemilineage decoded at 0.97–0.99 (k≥5); silhouette 0.29 (λ=1, k=5) vs 0.06 raw Y. Library/sex ≈ chance even in raw counts → this subset cannot test batch removal. No row offset → a depth factor appears at k≥5 (ρ≈0.56).

slides.title: D · Convergence
bullets: J monotone in all fits. λ≥3 converges in 10–190 iterations; 12/45 fits (all λ≤1) hit the 500-iteration cap. Restart spread ≤1e-5 at λ≥3, 1e-4–1e-2 at weak priors (distinct optima).

slides.title: D · Identifiability: unique up to rotation when well regularized
bullets: λ=1, k=5: raw U differs across seeds, but after Procrustes ≤1.6e-5 and P agrees to 3e-5. λ=0.3, k=10: different optima (|ΔP| up to 0.98). Orthogonal R leaves J unchanged; invertible A lowers J → prior removes all but O(k).

slides.title: D · Binarization sensitivity: count ≥ 1 vs ≥ 2
bullets: Same picture; ≥2 decodes hemilineage at lower rank and P carries more level information (gene-wise ρ 0.49). Best ≥2 model λ=3, k=10 (NLL 0.433).

slides.title: E · Synthetic ground truth: can data-only criteria find the true P?
bullets: S1 low-rank logistic (k*=3, 8) · S2 Poisson counts with clusters (misspecified) · S3 S2 + library batch (target P_bio). 3 seeds × 42 (λ, k).

slides.title: E · Evaluation criteria and the oracle
E · Criterion landscapes vs oracle
bullets: Oracle = KL(P_true ‖ P̂), the held-out NLL with infinitely many replicates.
C1 entry-CV, C2 count split, C3 replicate and C4 cell fold-in all put their minimum on the oracle optimum.
BIC always picks k=1; AIC/train NLL always k=20.

slides.title: E · Criterion vs oracle across the grid
bullets: C1 is a constant shift of the replicate experiment C3 (r ≥ 0.998): masked-entry CV is the runnable stand-in for a technical replicate.

slides.title: E · Model-selection regret
bullets: Exact oracle hits: C1 11/12 (one miss, +1.5% KL), C2 6/6, C3 12/12, C4 12/12; BIC/AIC 0/12 (regret 0.05–1.1 nats).

slides.title: E · Recovered vs true probabilities
bullets: Selected models: logit corr 0.96 / 0.92 / 0.84 / 0.83 (S1_k3 / S1_k8 / S2 / S3), well calibrated; weak priors over-confident, strong priors under-confident.

slides.title: E · Count splitting: right model, half-depth target
bullets: Poisson thinning gives two independent half-depth replicates (equations, slide 79). Use it to select (λ, k), then refit: KL 0.105 (half model) → 0.050 (depth-mapped) → 0.038 (full refit).

slides.title: E · Batch (S3): shrinkage and rank do not remove it
bullets: Selected model still decodes library at 0.70–0.74 (chance 0.25). Pushing library toward chance needs k≤3, which also destroys hemilineage. Batch needs explicit covariates.

slides.title: E · Convergence on synthetic grids
bullets: Near-optimal fits converge in 34–114 iterations; capped fits are high-k/weak-prior and far from optimal, so no argmin changes.
